question: What will be the percentage change in the British pound to US dollar exchange rate (GBPUSD=X on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-09-03 to the close on 2026-09-12?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-09-12 / close on 2026-09-03 - 1), using daily closes of GBPUSD=X on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-09-12, the last close before it is used.
baseline:
Computed by code from Yahoo Finance daily closes for GBPUSD=X: latest close 1.3532 on 2026-09-03.
Target date 2026-09-12 is 6 trading observations ahead. Percentiles of the price on the target date,
from the empirical distribution of 6-observation returns over the last 3 years (last year weighted double):
p5: 1.3332, p10: 1.337, p25: 1.3451, p50: 1.3536, p75: 1.3623, p90: 1.371, p95: 1.3765
This ignores news and known events; adjust for them. Check the symbol matches the resolution source
(exchange, contract month, close vs settlement price).
research:
I've finished searching and am now writing up the findings, using only information published by 2026-09-05.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-09-03: Yahoo Finance GBPUSD=X closed at **1.3532**, according to the code baseline. I couldn't open Yahoo directly, and the pages I tried to fetch were blocked by the proxy.
- 2026-09-03: For comparison, PoundSterlingLive shows 1.3514 for the day, within a range of about 1.3480 to 1.3548. Its Bank of England reference rate was 1.3518. The ~0.1% gap from Yahoo's figure probably comes from the time each source takes its "close". [PSL history](https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/GBP-USD-2026), [PSL BoE rates](https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/bank-of-england-spot/historical-spot-exchange-rates/gbp/gbp-to-usd-2026)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-09-04: PoundSterlingLive lists a close of about 1.3517, with a range of about 1.3485 to 1.3549. The BoE reference rate was about 1.3515 and ExchangeRates.org.uk shows 1.3517. [PSL](https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/GBP-USD-2026), [exchangerates.org.uk](https://www.exchangerates.org.uk/historical/find-exchange-rate-history-for-04_09_2026)
- If Yahoo's 4 Sep close is similar, the pair is about **-0.1%** against the 3 Sep reference, with 5 trading days left. Nothing has settled the question yet.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-04: US August payrolls came in at +162k against expectations of about 53k to 65k. It was the biggest gain since March. Unemployment stayed at 4.1% and hourly earnings rose 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y. July was revised up from -23k to +21k. CNBC reported that short-end Treasury yields rose sharply and traders added to bets on a Fed **hike** at the September meeting. This supports the dollar. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/jobs-report-august-2026.html), [CBS](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/august-jobs-report-us-labor-market/)
- Fed context: the Fed is in a possible tightening phase. Odds of a September hike fell after the weak July jobs report on 2026-08-07. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/odds-the-fed-hikes-in-september-tumble-following-big-july-jobs-miss.html) A Yahoo piece said September hike odds had risen above 50%, but I couldn't confirm its date. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/fomc-september-2026-odds-rate-201618784.html)
- 2026-08-21: GBP/USD hit about 1.3675, the high for August. Since then it has fallen roughly 1.2% to around 1.351. [exchangerates.org.uk](https://www.exchangerates.org.uk/GBP-USD-spot-exchange-rates-history-2026.html)
- UK: Bank Rate is 3.75%, and markets are debating whether the BoE will hike. I found no sterling-specific news from 3 to 5 September.

## 4. Base rates
- Code-computed distribution of the 6-trading-day outcome, starting from 1.3532:
  - p5: 1.3332 (-1.48%)
  - p10: 1.3370 (-1.20%)
  - p25: 1.3451 (-0.60%)
  - p50: 1.3536 (+0.03%)
  - p75: 1.3623 (+0.67%)
  - p90: 1.3710 (+1.32%)
  - p95: 1.3765 (+1.72%)
- In other words, a typical 6-day move is about ±0.65% (the middle half of outcomes) and about ±1.5% at the 5th and 95th percentiles. Results outside the question's -3% to +4% range would be very rare.
- Recent trend: since the 21 Aug high the pair has drifted lower, as the dollar firmed on Fed hike talk.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Robinhood runs daily prediction markets on GBP/USD, and its 4 Sep market used a threshold of about 1.3525. I couldn't find a market for 11 or 12 Sep, or its prices. [Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/us/en/prediction-markets/fx/events/pound-sterling-to-us-dollar-exchange-rate-september-4-2026-sep-04-2026/)
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this pair for this date, and no bank forecast for one week ahead published before 5 Sep.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **2026-09-11 (Fri), 8:30 ET: US August CPI.** This is the biggest scheduled risk, and it lands on the day that decides the question. With a Fed hike in play, it could move the pair a lot. [fedratecalc](https://fedratecalc.com/cpi-release-date/), [eco3min](https://eco3min.fr/en/next-us-cpi-release/)
- Around 10 to 11 Sep: UK monthly GDP for July should come out, but I couldn't confirm the date.
- The week of 7 Sep may bring US PPI and Fed comments before the blackout period for the mid-September FOMC meeting. I didn't check the dates.
- Just after the window: the FOMC meets around 15 to 16 Sep and the BoE MPC around 17 Sep. Positioning ahead of those meetings could affect the pair during the window.
